rv.q: This Threepenny Opera has many virtues, but it lacks the acrid bite and political urgency that should make Brecht's 1928 musical feel vital and dangerous.
While I've never heard a 'Threepenny' production that was better sung or played, the rough edges of Weill's score have been blunted in the process.
This is one party where the hangover begins almost as soon as the evening does.
